title: Memories of the Depression and World War II
summary: He had no sense of the Depression as a toddler and remembers wartime cartoons of Hitler at age eleven.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years

blocks.x: What’s your recollection of the Depression? Do you remember it as a depression?

No, not at all. I used to be up and down 135th Street, but I had no realization of it being a depression or anything, because I was a little baby boy at that point. I had my area that I could play in, because my godfather, Norman Cobbs, lived in the Y. We lived, my mother – the first place we lived, when she brought me up from North Carolina, was 135th Street, between Seventh and Lenox. So the house that I lived in was here, and the Y was here, where Daddy Cobbs was, and I had a stretch of sidewalk that I could go in, when the sidewalk was light brown. Then it turned grey. Once it got to the end of the light brown, I couldn’t go any further over that line. I had to come back, play down that end.
What about your recollection of World War II, of those years?
Yeah, I remember that, because I was, I guess, 11. I remember seeing Hitler, Mussolini, and Hirohito. Cartoons, they were making them look funny. I just knew that
they were bad guys that was doing something terrible to my country and that kind of thing that you have when you’re a kid, seeing all those movies, with the Americans fighting the Germans.
